method.read: Four full native PromQL avg_over_time() queries, 3 daily instants, per-case independent ALP/ZSTD1/ZSTD1/ALP and ALP/LZ4/LZ4/ALP, 2 warmups +8 measured queries per phase. QueryFinish wall, CPU, RSS snapshots, marks/rows, sampled processor + disjoint CPU stacks; all JSON labels/time/floats compared with default codec oracle.
method.write: One unpaired ingestion and one OPTIMIZE FINAL per table, process-wide CPU start/end snapshots and wall; NOT a write/merge CPU ABBA or steady workload; do not assign process CPU solely to codec.
method.validity: No OOM, all eight codec-pair ABBA p50/CPU baseline drift <=25%, full native result parity, all 2,488,320 values and 86,688 buckets per table and identical tag digest. Actual samples.value codec in SHOW CREATE verified. Input SHA and binary SHA verified.

source_mechanism: Default TimeSeries v11 SAMPLES uses `CODEC samples.timestamp (Delta,T64,ZSTD(3))` and `CODEC samples.value (ALP,ZSTD(3))`, and allows inner CODEC override in stock source StorageTimeSeries.cpp lines 1055-1117.
ALP is lossless floating-point transform; ZSTD1 and LZ4 are also lossless for Float64. All 2,488,320 sample elements and exact native numeric results matched.

On this synthetic small-range gauge wave dataset, ZSTD(1) stores SAMPLES 35.62% smaller than ALP+ZSTD3, LZ4 28.85% smaller, with identical bucket rows and marks; compressed read bytes also fall on broad selector.

Matched performance crosses over: ZSTD1 namespace CPU +9.96% vs A/A CPU drift 0.80% (robust regression) despite smaller physical data; broad-node CPU -6.10% vs A/A CPU drift 3.85% (potential but modest); pod-broad CPU -5.74% vs drift 8.42% (inconclusive); burst CPU+4.45% vs drift6.64% (inconclusive).
LZ4 mostly changes CPU by <3.3% near A/A drift in tested cases. No stable universal speedup.
Cross-run R17 host model was AMD EPYC 9V74, this R18 runner is AMD EPYC 9V45; do not compare absolute R17/R18 p50/CPU across these runners. All R18 codec comparisons are same runner.
limitations: One synthetic aligned Kubernetes gauge input with deterministic value pattern. It is not production noise, counter resets, sparse NaN/Inf, realistic jitter or high-cardinality 14d CI.
No concurrent 1/4/8 client performance; server has stock O1/glibc rather than optimized jemalloc ClickHouse. Do not infer production global codec tradeoff or VM parity.
Single unpaired write and one optimize per codec: descriptive wall/CPU snapshots only. Natural rolling inserts/merges, write amplification and cold tier not measured.
Output parity of native PromQL and matching sample-element counts, not independent byte-for-byte raw sample-array values after all merges; lossless codec contract is source-defined.
CPU hot stack categories from one representative query per arm are diagnostic, not median or causal per-function work; pipeline may cause nonlocal CPU changes.
Number of SAMPLES rows and marks does not change in this sample; the value codec does change compressed bytes, which can affect read caching.

invalid_first_run.reason: SHOW CREATE prints backticks on samples.value and expands Delta to Delta(8); first parser required unquoted Delta token, rejected correct default DDL before ingest. Corrected normalizer removed backticks and accepted Delta(8). No ClickHouse data or speed result from first run.

next_action: R18 dependent follow-up with orthogonal value distributions (constant, monotonic, high-entropy random finite, counter resets) on same 400-node R01 label/timestamp shape to decide whether ALP loses storage only on repeated low-range gauges. Require independent exact value hashes, true codec effective DDL, same-runner A/B/B/A and write/merge under naturally repeated updates. Prefer cheap preflight simulation/source math before another runner. Do not alter TimeSeries global default from current case.
